content: 1. Hormonal contraceptives may be affected by certain medications. If avoiding these interactions is not possible, it is recommended to use an additional effective non-hormonal contraceptive method during the period of co-administration and for 28 days after discontinuation of the interacting medication. 2. Aldesleukin can increase the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache is recommended. 3. Amikacin may decrease the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. An alternative or additional form of birth control may be necessary during concurrent use. 4.
